open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: What authoritative time source supplies `marked_at` when the deliverer creates a publication mark?
options: the host wall clock read directly
a time supplied by the calling flow
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected system clock backend owned by the service.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Is `marked_at` stored as naive UTC, offset-aware UTC, another timezone, or another canonical representation?
open_points.default_guess: Store UTC without an offset, matching the product's existing datetime convention.

open_points.subject: publication-mark operation
open_points.text: The calling flow reports the `photo_id` right after `photo.publish` answers, and the deliverer creates the mark.
open_points.question: How many readings of the time source may one mark operation take, at what step is the reading made, and is the same reading retained across retries or durable-write steps?
options: read exactly once after validation and use that value for the whole operation
allow multiple readings and store the final one
open_points.default_guess: Read exactly once after all refusal checks and before constructing the new mark; use that instant throughout the write.

open_points.subject: INV-10 required test
open_points.text: with every opening of the photo folder of that connection and of a file in it other than the connections file recorded, none is recorded
open_points.question: If the configured connections file is located inside the project's photo folder, does opening directories solely to reach that file count as a forbidden opening of the photo folder, or is the entire traversal needed for the mandatory connection-file read exempt?
options: exempt the directory traversal used only to read the connections file
count every photo-folder opening and therefore make such an operation fail the test
open_points.default_guess: Forbid placing the connections file inside any connected photo folder.

witness.initial: An unconfirmed project connection whose configured connections file is located inside that connection's photo folder.
events: The caller sends an authenticated scan, placement or mark request.
The service performs the connection check required by A5 rule 7 and opens directories leading through the photo folder to read the connections file exactly once.
outcomes: The directory opening counts as an opening of the photo folder, so the required INV-10 test fails even though the service accessed only the mandatory connections file.
The connections-file exemption includes the traversal needed to reach it, so the required INV-10 test passes.
witness.observer: The generated INV-10 check and its filesystem-open recorder

open_points.subject: INV-10 required test
open_points.text: a file in it other than the connections file
open_points.question: Is the connections-file exception determined by the configured pathname, by the opened file's identity, or by its content or role, especially when hard links or aliases exist?
options: only the configured connections-file pathname is exempt
every pathname resolving to the same file identity is exempt
the test fixture must prohibit aliases and hard links
open_points.default_guess: Exempt only the exact configured pathname and prohibit aliases in the test fixture.

witness.initial: The configured connections file has a second hard-link name inside the project's photo tree.
events: An unconfirmed-project operation reads the configured connections-file pathname.
A defective implementation also opens the second hard-link name while traversing photo content.
The test recorder classifies the opened objects.
outcomes: Path-based identity treats the second name as an ordinary photo file and detects the forbidden access.
Inode-based identity treats the second name as the connections file and silently exempts the forbidden access.
